key_insight: ATLAS makes fine-tuning input-conditioned by using retained-domain activation geometry to control a low-rank residual, helping a model learn new skills without rewriting unrelated behavior.
engineering_relevance: For constitutive-modeling-style workflows, this suggests a practical way to specialize a shared surrogate or operator while preserving previously validated responses and reducing regression risk.
method: Build an activation atlas from retained-domain representations to define local reference centers.
Use directional filters from the atlas to condition a shared low-rank residual during training and inference.
Train on task supervision while constraining updates through retained-domain geometry to limit off-task drift.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3-8B, ATLAS reports the lowest mean retained-output KL divergence among seven published baselines at matched coding performance, with consistent gains across multiple random seeds and broader tests on five backbones and two retained domains.
watch_item: The added atlas conditioning and decoding overhead are modest, but deployment still needs careful storage management and validation that the retained-domain atlas remains representative as tasks or domains change.
paper_title: Learn Here, Move Less Elsewhere: Input-Conditioned Plasticity from Retained-Domain Activation Atlases
